## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? ---PROMPT--- I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.
There's an ideas folder. Let me check it. Also read the runtime AGENTS.md and default-start to know how apps are served and what the framework expectations are.

Use `font-family: 'Trebuchet MS', ...` and text shadows for playful look.) `src/main.js` — boot, renderer, scene, camera, game loop, input. `src/world.js` — build level, materials, environment, helpers for meshes. `src/player.js` — player mesh creation + animation, physics state. `src/audio.js` — WebAudio SFX and light music loop (maybe simple upbeat arpeggio). Music toggle. Keep it pleasant, low volume. Generate chiptune-ish melody loop with oscillators scheduled via setInterval? Implement a simple sequencer using AudioContext currentTime scheduling with lookahead. Music adds polish. Mute button. `src/level.js` — data structure: platforms, coins, enemies, moving platforms, springs, checkpoints, goal. Game mechanics: - Move, jump, double jump? Mario has single jump + special; keep single jump with coyote time, variable height (release early cuts jump), jump buffer. Long jump? Add sprint (Shift) increases speed. Triple jump complexity skip. - Spin attack (E / click) to defeat nearby enemies? Add ground pound (Ctrl) maybe. Keep controls simple: WASD/arrows, Space jump, Shift run, mouse orbit, scroll zoom; mobile joystick + jump. - Stomp enemies, bounce. - Collect 100 coins? Count coins and star. Goal flag win. Total coins maybe 60. - 3 hearts; enemy contact loses heart with invincibility; fall respawns at last checkpoint with heart loss? Fall respawn no heart loss to be forgiving, but reset position. - Checkpoint flags activate and glow. - Timer counts up; win screen shows time, coins, rank (S/A/B) based on coins/time. Level layout (world units ~ 1 unit; player height 1.6, speed 6-9): Start island around origin at y=0, radius 7. Spawn (0, 0.2, 0). Path heading -Z (north) with jumps: 1. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D Mario-style platformer in the blank PlayGround repo, without asking clarifying questions.

## Requirements
- "make 3D Mario-style platformer" — complete playable game, reasonable assumptions allowed, briefly note assumptions when finished.
- Browser game; must be verified with a real browser screenshot and work responsively/mobile.

## Decisions
- Built "SUPER CLOUD HOP 3D" with Three.js + Vite, low-poly cartoon sky-island theme.
- Features: third-person camera, WASD/arrow movement, mouse-drag orbit, wheel zoom, jumping with coyote time/jump buffer/variable height, sprint, coins, question blocks, springs, moving platforms, goomba enemies, 3-hit Mega Goomba boss, checkpoints, goal flag, 3 lucky stars, hearts, timer, ranks, pause/restart, win/lose screens, WebAudio SFX/music, touch joystick/jump.
- One substantial course: Cloudtop Cascade, ~75 coins, 3 stars, 3 checkpoints, boss + goal.
- Added rectangular AABB platform collision and one-way-style landing checks; spring launches and stomp bounces are exempt from variable-jump cut.
- Optimized draw calls from ~931 to ~324–348 by merging static geometry (goombas' heads, flowers, clouds, coins, distant islands, tufts) and vertex-coloring merged meshes.
- Checkpoint flags moved off-center and trigger radius increased to 3 units for fewer camera obstructions and easier activation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Vite/Three.js project scaffold; `index.html`, full CSS UI, game modules.
- Core gameplay and systems implemented and functionally verified via deterministic `game.update(1/60)` stepping.
- Verified: movement, jump (~2.3 units), landing, 2 coins picked up, stomp (+1 coin, no damage), boss 3-stomp defeat (+5 coins), checkpoint activation/spawn, question block, spring launch (peak ~14.5), high-island landing, star pickup (+5 coins/heal), fall respawn, lose flow, retry, win screen, audio context starts on Play.
- Fixed duplicate HTML `id="result-stars"` bug; win screen now shows 2/3 earned star icons, correct stats and rank.
- Mobile HUD fits at 390px; title touch hints replace keyboard hints on coarse pointers.
- Favicon added; no browser console errors in normal play.
- Dev server running in tmux session `cloudhop` on `http://localhost:3002`.

### Active
- Final visual QA screenshots at goal/high-island were accidentally taken while paused, so they only show the pause overlay; need to re-capture gameplay views.
- Not yet committed; working tree changes are uncommitted.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Re-open/reload the game, click `#play-btn`, then capture gameplay screenshots at goal/high island without pausing:
   - teleport `19,7.1,-108`, `cameraState.yaw=0`, `pitch=0.3`, `snapCamera()`
   - teleport `0,12.1,-81`, `pitch=0.35`
2. Inspect visuals for occlusion/quality; adjust flag/goal/camera if needed.
3. Run a final production build (`npm run build`), reload and smoke-test start → move → jump → pause/resume, plus mobile layout.
4. Add/refresh a concise project README or final notes including assumptions (single course, procedural assets, synthesized audio).
5. Commit changes (currently uncommitted), e.g. `git add -A && git commit -m "Build Super Cloud Hop 3D platformer"`.
6. Final response: brief summary of the game, controls, verification performed, assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: core physics, collisions, enemies/boss, camera, win/lose, scoring, particles.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: level layout, islands, coins, springs, flags, boss, sky/clouds, merged scenery, platform sprites, spawns, checkpoint positions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/character.js`: hero rig and optimized merged-geometry goomba boss models.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: renderer setup, UI callbacks, game loop, debug API `window.__cloudHop`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: keyboard/mouse/touch input and joystick.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: HUD, title/pause/win/lose overlays, touch controls.

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()

const out = '/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots'
mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true })
const url = 'http://localhost:3002/'
const browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 })
const failures = []
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } })
page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
page.on('pageerror', e => failures.push('pageerror: ' + e.message))
page.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') failures.push('console: ' + m.text()) })
page.on('response', r => { if (r.status() >= 400 && new URL(r.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${r.status()}: ${r.url()}`) })
await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load' })
await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
await page.waitForTimeout(500)
await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, 'title.png') })

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'PLAY GAME' }).click()
await page.waitForTimeout(1200)

// start area
await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, 'game1.png') })

const snap = async (name, x, y, z, yaw, pitch) => {
  await page.evaluate(([x, y, z, yaw, pitch]) => {
    const g = window.__cloudHop.game
    window.__cloudHop.teleport(x, y, z)
    g.cameraState.yaw = yaw
    g.cameraState.pitch = pitch
    g.snapCamera()
  }, [x, y, z, yaw, pitch])
  await page.waitForTimeout(700)
  await page.screenshot({ path: join(out, name) })
}

console.log('state', JSON.stringify(await page.evaluate(() => window.__cloudHop.state)))
console.log('failures', JSON.stringify(failures))
await browser.close()

# SUPER CLOUD HOP 3D

A complete little Mario-style 3D platformer that runs in the browser. Hop across floating cloud islands, grab coins and Lucky Stars, bounce off springs, stomp goombas, and take down the three-hit Mega Goomba before raising the flag at the end of **Cloudtop Cascade**.

Built with [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) and [Vite](https://vitejs.dev/). Every model, texture, and sound is generated procedurally — there are no external art or audio assets.

## Play

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # http://localhost:3002
```

Production build:

```bash
npm run build
npm run preview
```

The build uses a relative base (`--base ./`), so `dist/` can be served from any static path.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard / mouse | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | `WASD` or arrow keys | Left joystick |
| Jump / stomp | `Space` | `JUMP` button |
| Sprint | `Shift` | Push joystick to the edge |
| Orbit camera | Drag with the mouse | Drag the sky |
| Zoom camera | Mouse wheel | Pinch / wheel |
| Pause | `Esc` or `P` | Pause button |
| Mute | `M` or speaker button | Speaker button |

The hero has coyote time, a jump buffer, and variable jump height, so short taps give small hops and held jumps go higher. Landing on a goomba bounces you; touching one from the side costs a heart.

## The course

- **Cloudtop Cascade** — one hand-built course of floating grass islands, stone steps, bridges, moving platforms, and a spring that launches you to the high island.
- **75 coins**, **3 Lucky Stars** (each worth +5 coins and a heal), and **3 checkpoints**.
- **Mega Goomba** boss with three hit points, a boss health bar, and a stomp cooldown.
- A finish flag, course timer, heart health, results screen with coin/time/star stats, and an `S`–`C` rank.

Falling off the islands costs a heart and respawns you at the last checkpoint. Losing all three hearts ends the run; clearing the course shows your results.

## Technical notes

- `src/game.js` — fixed-step physics, AABB collisions, checkpoints, enemies/boss, camera, scoring, and win/lose flow.
- `src/world.js` — level layout, pickups, props, sky, clouds, and merged static geometry.
- `src/character.js` — the hero rig and low-poly goomba/boss models.
- `src/input.js` — keyboard, mouse, touch joystick, and jump input.
- `src/audio.js` — synthesized WebAudio sound effects and looping music.
- `src/main.js` — renderer, UI wiring, game loop, and the `window.__cloudHop` test hook.

Assumptions: this is a single self-contained course rather than a full world map, progress is not saved between sessions, and the game is designed for modern desktop and mobile browsers with WebGL.

-# PlayGround
+# SUPER CLOUD HOP 3D
+
+A complete little Mario-style 3D platformer that runs in the browser. Hop across floating cloud islands, grab coins and Lucky Stars, bounce off springs, stomp goombas, and take down the three-hit Mega Goomba before raising the flag at the end of **Cloudtop Cascade**.
+
+Built with [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) and [Vite](https://vitejs.dev/). Every model, texture, and sound is generated procedurally — there are no external art or audio assets.
+
+## Play
+
+```bash
+npm install
+npm run dev      # http://localhost:3002
+```
+
+Production build:
+
+```bash
+npm run build
+npm run preview
+```
+
+The build uses a relative base (`--base ./`), so `dist/` can be served from any static path.
+
+## Controls
+
+| Action | Keyboard / mouse | Touch |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Move | `WASD` or arrow keys | Left joystick |
+| Jump / stomp | `Space` | `JUMP` button |
+| Sprint | `Shift` | Push joystick to the edge |
+| Orbit camera | Drag with the mouse | Drag the sky |
+| Zoom camera | Mouse wheel | — |
+| Pause | `Esc` or `P` | Pause button |
+| Mute | `M` or speaker button | Speaker button |
+
+The hero has coyote time, a jump buffer, and variable jump height, so short taps give small hops and held jumps go higher. Landing on a goomba bounces you; touching one from the side costs a heart.
+
+## The course
+
+- **Cloudtop Cascade** — one hand-built course of floating grass islands, stone steps, bridges, moving platforms, and a spring that launches you to the high island.
+- **75 coins**, **3 Lucky Stars** (each worth +5 coins and a heal), and **3 checkpoints**.
+- **Mega Goomba** boss with three hit points, a boss health bar, and a stomp cooldown.
+- A finish flag, course timer, heart health, results screen with coin/time/star stats, and an `S`–`C` rank.
+
+Falling off the islands costs a heart and respawns you at the last checkpoint. Losing all three hearts ends the run; clearing the course shows your results.
+
+## Technical notes
+
+- `src/game.js` — fixed-step physics, AABB collisions, checkpoints, enemies/boss, camera, scoring, and win/lose flow.
+- `src/world.js` — level layout, pickups, props, sky, clouds, and merged static geometry.
+- `src/character.js` — the hero rig and low-poly goomba/boss models.
+- `src/input.js` — keyboard, mouse, touch joystick, and jump input.
+- `src/audio.js` — synthesized WebAudio sound effects and looping music.
+- `src/main.js` — renderer, UI wiring, game loop, and the `window.__cloudHop` test hook.
+
+Assumptions: this is a single self-contained course rather than a full world map, progress is not saved between sessions, and the game is designed for modern desktop and mobile browsers with WebGL.
+
